newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Suriname, Venezuela agree closer cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Suriname, Venezuela agree closer cooperation.

text.p: The presidents of Surinam and Venezuela agreed on Thursday to promote closer cooperation between their countries.

Suriname's President Jules Wijdenbosch, who arrived in Venezuela Wednesday for a three-day official visit, said they saw opportunities to join forces on energy, housing, the fight against drug trafficking and other issues.
"We have committed ourselves to study joint action in a few specific areas," Wijdenbosch told a news conference at Miraflores presidential palace.
Wijdenbosch, who won a tight presidential run-off in the former Dutch colony last September, signed a joint statement with Venezuela's President Rafael Caldera.
It included a commitment to hold a meeting in Surinam before July "to discuss and agree on measures to efficiently advance the fight" against drug trafficking.
Wijdenbosch, whose National Democratic Party is backed by former military strongman Desi Bouterse, declined to answer questions about Bouterse's role in his government.
"It is not my duty to reply to these questions," he said.
Bouterse, who staged two coups and led a military government in the 1980s, is currently in China as the president's special envoy.
